title: chart-options.json
description: The options of each chart that the model can set, and the version of each panel. The Renderer build writes this file.

panels.description: The key is a panel ID of registry/panel-types.json.

charts.description: The key is a chart name of registry/chart-types.json.

pluginVersion.description: The version of the panel: info.version of its built plugin.json. A version of Semantic Versioning 2.0.0, for example 0.4.1.

options.description: The panel options. A path starts at the options object of the panel.

fieldConfig.description: The field options. A path starts at fieldConfig.defaults of the panel. It is also the id of an override property.

path.description: The names of the keys from the root object to the value, joined with dots, for example legend.placement.

description.description: What the option changes in the chart, in one line.

tier.description: advanced is an option that few charts need.

default.description: The value that the Renderer uses when the panel does not have the option. It validates against schema. With no default, the Renderer decides.

valueSchema.description: The JSON Schema of the value of an option. It uses only these keywords, and it has no reference.

type.description: One type, or a list of types for a value that can have more than one, for example a number or null.

anyOf.description: The value validates against one or more of these schemas, for example a boolean or a number with a minimum.

tool-result.$defs.panelId.$comment: Generated from registry/panel-types.json. Do not edit.

query-datasource-args.properties.type.$comment: Generated from registry/chart-types.json. Do not edit.
query-datasource-args.properties.type.description: Optional chart to draw. With no type, the chart comes from the data. Each chart needs: timeseries (a time field and number fields), barchart (number fields, with a string or time field for the categories), histogram (number fields), candlestick (number fields named open, high, low and close), boxplot (number fields named min, q1, median, q3 and max), piechart (a number field, with a string field for the names of the parts), funnel (a number field, with a string field for the names of the stages), heatmap (heatmap cells, or a time field and number fields for the buckets), geomap (a geo field, a geohash field, or latitude and longitude fields), state-timeline (a time field and string, boolean or number fields), status-history (a time field and string, boolean or number fields), nodeGraph (node graph frames, or source and target fields), sankey (source, target and value fields), chord (source, target and value fields), treemap (string fields for the levels and a number field), sunburst (string fields for the levels and a number field), radar (three or more number fields), parallel (two or more number fields), streamgraph (a time field and number fields), bubble (a time field and number fields), gauge (1 to 10 number fields; a reducer gives one value for each field, by default the last value), stat (1 to 10 number fields; a reducer gives one value for each field, by default the last value).
